clue.text: They conduct recces with balletic finesse

indicators.note: finesse is skilful handling, so the words before it are deftly rearranged

parts.note: first part of the letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Dancers go on reconnaissance missions with the grace of the ballet stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conduct' suggests leading people, but here it means carrying electricity. A recce is British slang for a reconnaissance trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Wires that carry current are conductors, so they conduct electricity from place to place.

clue.text: He works to know how know-how works

definitions.text: He works to know how know-how works

parts.words: He works to know how know-how works
parts.note: surface reading: a curious worker trying to understand how skill operates
setter's reading: someone who studies the nature of knowledge itself, a philosopher of the theory of knowing

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'know how' makes it sound like a practical skill; the person meant studies epistemology, the branch of philosophy about how we know things.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistemology is the philosophical study of knowledge, and its practitioner examines how understanding is acquired.

clue.text: Authorise setter to raise strength

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker is given authority to build up their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant someone official powers or permission is to authorise them.

clue.text: Allowed to be carried outside 50 times

indicators.note: the word for carried sits on the outside, wrapping round the other pieces

parts.note: to tote is to carry
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something may be carried out of a place, but only fifty times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried outside' reads as taken out; here the word for carried is split open to wrap round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerated is put up with or permitted, the same sense as allowed.

clue.text: Dead one (a sloth)

parts.note: lifeless, motionless
Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lifeless creature, identified in brackets as a sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'sloth' look like the animal; it is the word for laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness or reluctance to move, which is a state of inactivity.

clue.text: Large number cotton on to Old World leader

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
lint is cotton fluff or fabric
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty of people catch on to an ancient ruler's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old World' looks like Europe and Asia; it means a former world leader, a past US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton was US president in the 1990s, once a leading figure on the global stage.

clue.text: The French speak up for bread

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the French masculine article
to gab is to chatter

explanation.surface: French people speak out in favour of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped roll, a kind of bread that is boiled then baked.

clue.text: Passed up drink, then sped about

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the next word runs bottom to top

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and jumbled

parts.note: the four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone turned down a drink and then raced around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed up' reads as declined; the definition is only 'Passed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by, as when hours have passed.

clue.text: Missive left by Miss: "I've left …"

parts.note: surface reading: a note a young woman left behind
setter's reading: a note in which a woman tells her partner the relationship is over

explanation.walkthrough: The play on 'left' twice and 'Missive'/'Miss' hides a break-up note; the name in it is the traditional one for a jilted man.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the idiom for a letter from a woman ending a romance, originally with soldiers overseas.

clue.text: Drive child to University College in London

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
standard abbreviation
the London School of Economics, a college of the University of London

explanation.surface: Take a child to University College London by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University College in London' reads as UCL, the real institution; it splits into U and LSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is an urge or motivating force, the sense of drive as inner push.

clue.text: "See the Ashes here?" He says: "No thanks"

definitions.meaning: first reading: where ashes lie, split as ..., in the fireplace
second meaning: an ungrateful person who gives no thanks

explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket trophy, an urn; here ashes are just fire remains, found in the grate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person who fails to show gratitude is someone who withholds thanks.

clue.text: Wrote off for a tug

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sent off a letter asking for a tugboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as 'one who tows', not a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a boat that pulls other vessels, so it is something that tows.

clue.text: Change ratio — let's share winnings depending on stake here

definitions.text: share winnings depending on stake here

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Gamblers propose altering the payout ratio so winnings are split according to bets.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote's machine pools all bets and divides the pot among winners in proportion to their stakes.

clue.text: Writer of note: "I want novel!"

parts.note: a mark is a note or sign

indicators.note: novel means new, so the words before it take a new form

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A famous author demands a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being asked for; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American author of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: A receiver at Trade Centre 10

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the middle three letters
the digits 1 and 0 read as letters

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a parcel at Trade Centre number 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade Centre 10' looks like an address; it is the middle of trade followed by 10 written as I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set picks up broadcast signals, so it is a receiving device.

clue.text: The majority to mediate and rig votes

indicators.note: the majority of a word is most of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to referee is to arbitrate between parties

indicators.note: to rig is to fix or tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The majority want to arbitrate and fix ballots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The majority' sounds like the electorate; it trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public ballots in which the whole electorate decides a single question.

clue.text: Black and blue snake taken from Bolivia to Germany

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes those letters from it

parts.note: taken as written
a boa is a constricting snake
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A bruised snake is smuggled from South America to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters of the snake are scattered in Bolivia: B and O at the front, A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid literally means bruise-coloured, the bluish-black shade of a battered body.

clue.text: Disappear with Russian leader in Japan

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter counts

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A Russian leader goes missing in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like the country; as a verb it means to coat with hard glossy lacquer.
explanation.definitionFit: To japan is to coat with black lacquer, a kind of varnish, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: He can't if I become leader

indicators.note: to become is to turn into something else, so the letters are transformed

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rival boasts that someone else cannot succeed if they take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a clan or tribe, its ruling figure.

clue.text: Students here see old King take stage

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Old King Cole, the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Students watch an aged monarch step onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old King' is not a past monarch but the nursery-rhyme character in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of learning where students study and often live.

clue.text: Understanding things I compile

indicators.note: to compile is to assemble from parts, so the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on grasping the material they gather together.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep grasp of a situation, the noun sense of understanding.

clue.text: With flower, topless model causes offence

indicators.note: without its top, a down word loses its first letter

parts.note: the saffron crocus, a flower
the Ford Model T

explanation.surface: A glamour model posing topless with a flower shocks the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' applies to the flower, not the model.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an insult or slight, something that gives offence.

clue.text: They might be seen spouting at church

definitions.text: They might be seen spouting at church

parts.note: surface reading: preachers holding forth in a church
setter's reading: carved stone waterspouts on a church roof pouring out rainwater

explanation.walkthrough: 'spouting' suggests long-winded speech; it is literal, water gushing from carved mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: These grotesque stone figures on churches serve as drainpipes, throwing rainwater clear of the walls.

clue.text: Flintoff — a Lancastrian displaying heart, perhaps

indicators.note: displaying means showing what is inside, so the letters are on view within the words

parts.note: found across the end of the cricketer's name and the next word

explanation.surface: Cricketer Andrew Flintoff, a Lancashire man, shows great heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Flintoff played cricket for Lancashire and England; the heart is the organ, not courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart is one of the organ meats, which together are called offal, so it is an example.

clue.text: Plunder from chamber if left unattended

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third
surface padding completing the picture of a room left unguarded

explanation.surface: Your room may be ransacked if you leave it unguarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unattended' completes the burglary picture and plays no part in the wordplay; 'chamber' also hints at a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search through and steal, as thieves ransack a drawer.

clue.text: Small vessel left England to this music

parts.note: a skiff is a small rowing boat
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A little boat sailed from England with music playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as departed; it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiffle is a 1950s British folk-jazz style played on homemade instruments like washboards.

clue.text: A source of seashells?

parts.note: surface reading: a beach where shells are found
setter's reading: artillery shells fired at sea from a small armed vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The shells are explosive rounds, not molluscs' homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small warship carrying heavy guns fires shells out on the water.

parts.note: the answer to 5 is a surname; Chelsea is a famous bearer of it, the president's daughter
the answer to 11 is one that tows, and a tractor is such a vehicle

explanation.surface: A bare sum: five plus eleven equals four times four.
explanation.walkthrough: The arithmetic is a decoy. Chelsea is a wealthy London district, and a Chelsea tractor is British slang for a big SUV used on city streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-by-four is a four-wheel-drive vehicle, the SUV mocked by this slang.
